title: The One Detail That Makes Fiction Feel Real
lesson: Small, ordinary details make a fictional world feel inhabited: what people eat, how they greet strangers, what they do when it rains.

voice.direction: Warm, thoughtful, conversational; intimate and observant, never dramatic. Slightly curious on the hook. Gentle emphasis on 'upside down'. Clear and deliberate on the three examples (food, greetings, habits). Confident but natural on the CTA.

lines.text: You don't need to describe an entire kingdom to make it believable.
In this town, when the first rain falls, everyone turns their doorstep bowl upside down.
Children learn it before they can read.
Food hints at climate. Greetings, at culture. Habits, at history.
Small, ordinary details tell us this world has a life beyond the story.
Follow for practical worldbuilding techniques, not just lore dumps.
